name: Slieve Russell Hotel Golf & Country Club
shortDesc: Four-star country resort set on 300 acres of gardens, lakes and golf course, with multiple restaurants, a spa, pool and walking trails.

name: Lough Rynn Castle
shortDesc: Historic 19th-century Tudor Revival castle hotel on a 300-acre lakeside estate, with grand period interiors, restored walled gardens and a surprisingly turbulent history.

name: Kilronan Castle
shortDesc: 19th-century castle on Lough Meelagh with woodland walks and spa.

name: Hotel Woodstock
shortDesc: Comfortable base on the edge of Ennis, handy for the Burren & Cliffs of Moher.

name: Dunboyne Castle Hotel
shortDesc: Georgian manor-style hotel with spa, an easy hop to/from Dublin.

name: Cliffs of Moher
shortDesc: Iconic sea cliffs with epic views.

name: Newgrange & Brú na Bóinne
shortDesc: Extraordinary 5,000-year-old passage tomb in the Brú na Bóinne World Heritage Site, famous for prehistoric art and a chamber aligned with the winter-solstice sunrise.

name: Cabra Castle
shortDesc: Historic castle hotel on a 100-acre estate beside Dún a’ Rí Forest Park.

name: Guinness Storehouse
shortDesc: Brewery tour ending at the Gravity Bar.

name: Carlow Castle
shortDesc: Ruined 13th-century Norman stronghold built for William Marshal, now famous for losing half its structure during a disastrous 1814 attempt to convert it into an asylum.

name: National Museum of Ireland – Archaeology
shortDesc: Ireland’s flagship archaeology museum on Kildare Street — home of the Ardagh Chalice, Tara Brooch, and bog bodies.

name: Trim Castle
shortDesc: Ireland’s largest Anglo-Norman castle, overlooking the River Boyne — famed for its medieval history and as a Braveheart filming location.

name: Carrickfergus Castle
shortDesc: Late-12th-century Norman stronghold on Belfast Lough; one of the best-preserved medieval castles in Northern Ireland.

name: Reginald’s Tower
shortDesc: Viking/Anglo-Norman round tower anchoring Waterford’s Viking Triangle; compact museum with artifacts and city views.

name: Lismore Castle
shortDesc: Private riverside castle and gardens on the Blackwater, home to the Duke of Devonshire and one of Ireland’s most picturesque estates.

name: Luttrellstown Castle
shortDesc: Grand Gothic/Georgian castellated house on a 560-acre estate just outside Dublin; famous for weddings and historic owners from the Luttrells to the Guinness family.

name: Dublin Castle
shortDesc: Seat of English/British rule in Ireland for centuries; today a state complex with guided tours, courtyard, chapel, and state apartments.

name: King John’s Castle
shortDesc: Impressive 13th-century Norman fortress on King’s Island in Limerick, restored with modern exhibits and commanding views of the River Shannon.

name: Malahide Castle
shortDesc: Furnished medieval-to-Georgian castle set in 260 acres of parkland near the sea; home to the Talbot family for nearly 800 years.

name: Maynooth Castle
shortDesc: 13th-century FitzGerald stronghold at the edge of Maynooth town; impressive ruins with guided tours in summer and easy access from Dublin.

name: Ashford Castle
shortDesc: Lavish 13th-century castle hotel on Lough Corrib; famed for its stone turrets, lakeside walks, and timeless luxury.

name: Trinity College – Book of Kells Experience
shortDesc: Ireland’s most famous manuscript and the Old Library’s Long Room, presented in a new immersive exhibition at Trinity College Dublin.

name: National Gallery of Ireland
shortDesc: Ireland’s premier art museum beside Merrion Square, with European masters and a superb Irish collection.

name: Kilkenny Castle
shortDesc: Magnificent Anglo-Norman castle turned stately home overlooking the River Nore; centerpiece of Kilkenny’s medieval cityscape.

name: The Rock of Cashel
shortDesc: Dramatic limestone outcrop crowned by medieval ecclesiastical buildings—round tower, Cormac’s Chapel, and vast cathedral ruins.

name: Rock of Dunamase
shortDesc: Spectacular hilltop ruins of a Norman stronghold near Portlaoise, offering sweeping views and a raw, untamed atmosphere.

name: Blarney Castle
shortDesc: Iconic medieval tower house near Cork, famous for the Blarney Stone and surrounded by 60 acres of lush gardens and grounds.

name: Ring of Kerry
shortDesc: Ireland’s most scenic drive, looping 179 km through mountains, lakes, and Atlantic coastline from Killarney through Kenmare and back.

name: Dunguaire Castle
shortDesc: Picturesque 16th-century tower house on Galway Bay with a walled bawn; coastal views toward the Burren.

name: Leap Castle
shortDesc: Privately owned 15th-century tower house near Roscrea, reputedly Ireland’s most haunted castle, still under restoration and open by appointment.

name: Clonony Castle
shortDesc: Early 16th-century Tudor-era tower house near Shannonbridge, once linked to the Boleyn family; privately owned and occasionally open for tours.

name: Dunlough Castle (Three Castles Head)
city: Three Castles Head, Mizen Peninsula (Co. Cork)
shortDesc: Spectacular 13th-century cliff-top ruin: three towers linked by curtain walls between a lake and the Atlantic cliffs at the tip of the Mizen.

name: Dunluce Castle
shortDesc: Clifftop medieval and Jacobean ruins above the North Atlantic, once home to the MacDonnell clan and one of the most dramatic castles in Ireland.

name: Cahir Castle
shortDesc: Massive 13th-century fortress on the River Suir; one of Ireland’s best-preserved castles, featuring towers, battlements, and film-worthy views.

name: Birr Castle Demesne
shortDesc: Historic seat of the Parsons family with gardens, science centre, and the Great Telescope—once the world’s largest.

name: Charleville Castle
shortDesc: Spectacular early-19th-century Gothic Revival castle in Charleville Forest; volunteer-led tours, restoration in progress, and famous ghost stories.

name: Athlone Castle
shortDesc: Restored 13th-century riverside fortress with modern visitor centre and views over the River Shannon and Athlone Bridge.

name: Howth Castle
shortDesc: Historic coastal estate and former home of the St. Lawrence family, occupied for over 800 years and set among gardens and forest trails overlooking Dublin Bay.

name: Ardgillan Castle
shortDesc: 18th-century country house with sea views over the Irish Sea, surrounded by parkland, rose gardens, and woodland walks north of Dublin.

name: Barberstown Castle
shortDesc: 13th-century fortified house turned luxury hotel near Straffan; combines medieval tower and 17th-century manor wings amid gardens and courtyards.

name: Tullynally Castle
shortDesc: Gothic Revival castle near Castlepollard with towers, gardens, and parklands; ancestral seat of the Pakenham family for over 350 years.

name: Castle Leslie Estate
shortDesc: Victorian country estate near Glaslough with a lakeside castle, gardens, and equestrian centre; family-run and famed for its warm hospitality.

name: Markree Castle
shortDesc: Gothic Revival castle near Sligo, once home to an observatory that discovered an asteroid; now a luxurious hotel surrounded by parkland and the River Unshin.

name: Enniskillen Castle
shortDesc: 15th-century riverside fortress on Lough Erne, now housing the Fermanagh County Museum and the Inniskillings Museum of military history.

name: Doe Castle
shortDesc: 15th-century tower house on Sheephaven Bay, once stronghold of the MacSweeney clan; surrounded by tidal waters and scenic coastal views.

name: Bunratty Castle
shortDesc: 15th-century tower house restored with period furnishings and surrounded by a living folk park recreating Irish village life from the 19th century.

name: Rathmullan Abbey
shortDesc: Ruins of a 16th-century Carmelite friary overlooking Lough Swilly, known as the departure point of the Flight of the Earls in 1607.

name: Knappogue Castle
shortDesc: 15th-century O’Brien clan tower house near Quin, restored as a residence with gardens and traditional medieval banquets.

name: Doonagore Castle
shortDesc: 16th-century round tower house above Doolin, overlooking the Atlantic and Aran Islands; one of the most photographed landmarks on Ireland’s west coast.

name: Leamaneh Castle
shortDesc: Ruined 15th-century tower house and 17th-century mansion in the Burren, once home to the O’Brien clan and the legendary 'Red Mary.'

name: Carrigaholt Castle
shortDesc: 15th-century coastal tower house guarding the Shannon estuary, built by the McMahon clan and linked to Grace O’Malley and the Spanish Armada.

name: Lough Eske Castle
shortDesc: Historic lakeside estate near Donegal Town, once tied to the O’Donnell clan; rebuilt in the 19th century and now a luxury castle hotel amid forests and mountains.

name: Kilkea Castle
shortDesc: 12th-century fortress and former Fitzgerald family stronghold near Castledermot; now a luxury hotel surrounded by woodlands and golf course.

name: Japanese Gardens – Irish National Stud
shortDesc: World-famous early 20th-century Japanese gardens at the Irish National Stud in Tully, symbolizing the ‘Life of Man’ through paths, bridges, and streams.

name: Ross Castle
shortDesc: 15th-century O’Donoghue stronghold on Lough Leane in Killarney National Park; restored tower house offering guided tours and lakeside views.

name: Cloghan Castle
shortDesc: Restored 13th-century Norman tower house near Loughrea, originally built by the Burke family; now a privately owned castle available for exclusive stays and events.

name: Ballynahinch Castle
shortDesc: 17th-century country estate in Connemara built on O’Flaherty clan lands, once owned by Grace O’Malley’s descendants; now a lakeside hotel amid the Twelve Bens mountains.

name: McDermott’s Pub
shortDesc: Beloved family-run pub in Doolin serving legendary fish and chips and hosting nightly traditional Irish music sessions.

name: Croagh Patrick & Murrisk Abbey
shortDesc: Sacred mountain known as 'The Reek' with a pilgrimage trail to St. Patrick’s summit chapel and the 15th-century ruins of Murrisk Abbey at its base.

name: Jaybees Bakery (Dunmore Road)
shortDesc: Beloved Amish-Mennonite bakery in a petrol station on the Dunmore Road; famed for brown bread, carrot cake, and a proper 99 ice cream.

name: Killarney Adventure & Nightlife
shortDesc: Spend the day paddling the Lakes of Killarney and touring Ross Castle before unwinding at J.M. Reidy’s for cocktails, live music, and local charm.

name: Cork City – Butter Museum & English Market
shortDesc: Ireland’s food capital — visit the Cork Butter Museum to learn the city’s creamy history, then sample local treats at the English Market.

name: Foxford Woollen Mills
shortDesc: Ireland’s historic mill (1892) still weaving blankets and scarves; tours, café, and a great shop for Irish knitwear and gifts.

name: The Burren Perfumery
shortDesc: Handmade perfumes & certified-organic creams made on site in the Burren; herb garden, tea rooms, and a lovely shop.

name: The Crosskeys Inn
shortDesc: Ireland’s oldest thatch-roof pub between Belfast and Derry, serving hearty fare, local whiskey, and live traditional music in a 17th-century setting.

name: Kennedy’s Pub
shortDesc: Classic Dublin pub near Merrion Square known for Irish stew, brown bread, and a cozy pint of Orchard Thieves cider.

name: The Fields Pub
shortDesc: Friendly Kilkenny local pub with live music, great pints, and a welcoming bartender named Mary.
